comments.text: My favorite thing about this show is that there's no music. No soundtrack to build tension or suspense. The moments are just happening, and we need to sit with them.

comments.author: @coreyrueckheim3881
comments.text: My wife and I loved to watch E.R. We named our son Noah, after Noah Wylie. Now its 22 years later and so much has happened since then, including divorce. But we've remained good friends. Sadly, she passed away three days ago from brain cancer. I will never be the same. I discovered this new show and I wish so much that I could watch it with her.

comments.text: This makes me really happy. ER doesn't get enough credit. It started the trend of great television.

comments.author: @dwkwb8
comments.text: This is the most accurate depiction of emergency medicine I have ever seen. It’s incredibly accurate.  Even the medical terminology and dosing is accurate.

comments.author: @msheehandub
comments.text: Physician suicide is real. The fact that you see two scenes, with two different doctors, standing at the edge of a building should be very very very unsettling for everyone. It's common for "frontline" healthcare workers to joke about this kind of thing but imagine any other profession joking about suicide like this. They nailed it with "pay a living wage and nurses will line up". CEO's and their friends are stealing lives from the people who actually make a difference by raking in millions while paying pennies.
